--- order: 6 unit: build assumes: [js-event, text-content, input-value] title: "A page that keeps score" summary: "Keep a number between clicks in a variable made above the handler, and use an if to decide when something happens." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 6 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: "A variable made above the handler keeps its value from click to click" clip: - caption: "The number on the page, and a button to raise it." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "

Clicks: 0

\n\n", append: true} - caption: "clicks is made above the handler, so it keeps its value between clicks." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 400 - click: {selector: "#click", preview: true} - click: {selector: "#click", preview: true} - click: {selector: "#click", preview: true} - expect: {selector: "#count", contains: "3", preview: true} - caption: "Three clicks, and the variable remembered each one." - wait: 750 hook: "How does a like counter remember 5 between one click and the next?" --- A page can **remember** things in variables, as your p5 sketches did. The rule is where you make them: ```js let clicks = 0; // made once, above the handler button.addEventListener("click", function () { clicks = clicks + 1; // changed on every click countEl.textContent = clicks; // shown on the page }); ``` A variable made **above** the handler keeps its value between clicks. One made **inside** is made again on each click, so it starts over. An `if` inside the handler decides when something happens, such as winning at 10. **The hard part** is seeing that the number on the page is not the memory. The variable remembers; the page only shows it. Change the variable, then show it. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict check: type: predict q: "After 3 clicks, what does the page show?" options: ["Clicks: 3", "Clicks: 0", "Clicks: 1", "Clicks: 111"] actual: "Clicks: 3. clicks is made once, above the handler. Each click adds 1 to the same variable, and the page shows the new value." ``` Is `clicks` made once, or on every click? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I clicked ten times and won, and I saw the button stop working." } ``` Press **Run** and click the button ten times. The `if` inside the handler decides when you win, and `button.disabled = true` stops the button. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "A variable made above the handler remembers between clicks, a variable made inside starts over; the page only shows the variable, so change it first, then show it." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each line with what it does." pairs: - ["let clicks = 0;", "makes the memory, once, above the handler"] - ["clicks = clicks + 1;", "changes the memory on every click"] - ["countEl.textContent = clicks;", "shows the memory on the page"] - ["if (clicks >= 10) { … }", "decides when to win"] - check: type: question q: "Why does the code change clicks first and then set the text?" options: ["The page only shows what the variable says, so the variable must change first", "JavaScript needs variables to be first", "The text would not change otherwise", "It is quicker"] answer: 0 explain: "The page does not know about clicks. It shows whatever you put in it. Change the variable, then put the new value on the page." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "The page shows 1 on every click and never goes higher. There is no red error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 6 fault: logic misconception: state-in-handler explain: "let clicks = 0 is inside the handler, so each click makes a new clicks that starts at 0. Make it above the handler, once." ``` ### Which line does what? Memory, change and show. ### Variable first The page is only a picture. ### Spot the bug The count never gets past 1. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Reset puts the variable and the page back; a second if reacts to a different number." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } tasks: - hint: - "A reset button needs to put back everything the game changed." - "Set clicks back to 0, show it on the page, and also put the message and the button back." expected: page.html#sol-reset check: { type: code, text: "Add a Reset button that starts the game again.", rules: { contains: ["clicks = 0"] } } - hint: - "The game already has one if. A second if can look for a different number." - "if (clicks === 5) { message.textContent = \"Halfway there!\"; } inside the handler." expected: page.html#sol-great check: { type: code, text: "Show Halfway there! when the count reaches 5.", rules: { contains: ["if (", "5"] } } ``` ### Reset Put everything back. ### Halfway A second if. ## Make: a clicker game of your own ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: a score that keeps its value, a goal, and a message when you win or lose." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I made a game with a score, a goal, and a message at the end." } ``` Make a small game: click a moving star, press as fast as you can, guess a number. It needs a **score variable** made above the handler, a **goal or a time limit**, and a **message** when you win or lose. It's the same running score as a micro:bit scoreboard or the console points counter, now kept between clicks. The page on this lesson moves a star and stops after 10 seconds, using `setInterval`. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "Your quiz needs a list of questions, a score and a click handler. What does the quiz keep in variables?" options: ["The current question number and the score", "The text of the page", "The buttons", "The CSS"] answer: 0 explain: "The quiz is a list of data plus a little memory: which question it is on, and how many were right. Next: the final challenge." ``` You can now keep a score. Next: **the final challenge**, a quiz page. ```teacher summary: Students keep a count in a variable made above a click handler, show it on the page, win at ten with an if, find a variable made inside the handler that starts over, and make a clicker game of their own. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can keep a number between clicks in a variable. - I can show a changing number on the page. - I can use an if inside a handler to decide when something happens. before: > Read the unit primer first. This is the Python "global" and state idea in JavaScript: a variable made above a function is shared and kept; one made inside is made again each call. The p5 sketches kept values in `let` above `draw`; here the handler plays the part of `draw`. The page is only a picture of the variable: change the variable, then put it on the page. The bug has no red error. `button.disabled = true` is a property like `textContent`. The Make example uses `setInterval` (run a function every 1000 ms) and `clearInterval`; students can use it as a recipe, and a number of them will want it. running: - 'Predict: ask students to say "made once" or "made each click" about clicks.' - "Run: ask where the number on the page comes from." - 'Investigate: for the bug, ask "how many times is let clicks run?"' - "Modify: ask what a reset must put back." - "Make: ask each student what the score is, what the goal is, and what happens at the end." stuck: - see: The count stays at 1. ask: Is the variable made inside the handler? fix: Move let clicks = 0 above the handler. - see: The count is right but the page does not change. ask: Is the new value put on the page? fix: Set countEl.textContent = clicks after changing clicks. - see: Reset does not fully reset. ask: What else did the game change besides clicks? fix: Put back the message and enable the button. - see: Cannot assign to a const. ask: Is the variable made with const and then changed? fix: Use let for a variable that changes. stretch: Make the goal change each game (a random target), or keep a best score that survives a reset. support: Give the counter and ask students for only the win message. leads: "Next lesson: the final challenge, a quiz page." exit: q: Why is let clicks above the handler and not inside it? a: Above, it is made once and keeps its value; inside, it would start over on every click. explain: | 1. A variable made above the handler keeps its value between clicks. 2. Change the variable first, then put it on the page with `textContent`. 3. An `if` in the handler decides when something happens. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-reset step-4#t2: page.html#sol-great step-5: page.html#sol-make struggle: The page shows the variable; it is not the variable. Ask "what does the page know about clicks?" and the answer is nothing. ```
